Our irrepressible Boys and Colts turned out in force and David Didino in the older age group looked most impressive with a 100 metre win in 13.5 and then twice improving the Championship Best in the High Jump.
H.Jump: · R.Hopkins (J) 1.88; C.Brooks 1.80; A.Bentt 1.78; D.Didino (B) 1.50; J.Martin 1.47

"Right, who's next" - Some of the Belgrave lads stand prepared to take on all-comers. Left to right: Gary Budinger, S.Watts, Mark Shippen, Robert Bashford, Steve Walters, Gary Wallace, David Didino and Ivan Beaumont.
Paul Warren and Danny Richards provided the other medallists with Adrian Cook and David Didino not competing in the necessary five events but nevertheless putting up some good performances.
The junior high jump gave David Didino the chance to launch himself to a new height of 1.67m and Richard Danpure, a new signing, set a championship best in winning the boys event.
Two youngsters also making promising first appearances were David Didino who reached 3rd in the 'B' high jump, and Michael Manning who gained a similar position in the 5,000 metres.
Youngsters, David Didino for example, are beginning to make their mark, and it is even rumoured that Arnold Bentt is going to train this winter.
Hopkins,Jnr. has firmly established himself and two more youngsters who have made auspicious beginnings in the event are Youths Ronnie McCrossen and David Didino.
The events pursued by the four from Belgrave were: Triple Jump - Ivan Beaumont, High Jump - David Didino, 800 metres - Richard Danpure, and myself - Javelin.
